questions.prompt: Convert rw-r----- to octal (digits as an integer). (tolerance 0.5)
With umask 022, what mode (octal digits as an integer) does a new directory requested with 777 get? (tolerance 0.5)
What is the octal mode of rwxrwxr-x? (integer digits, tolerance 0.5)
A script has mode 644 and starts with a correct shebang. What happens on ./script.sh?
options: It runs, but as root, because the shebang names the interpreter
It runs normally, because the shebang names a valid interpreter
Permission denied (status 126): there is no execute bit
Command not found (status 127): the path is not searched
questions.explanation: Execution requires an x bit; the shell reports 126.

questions.prompt: A command is not found in PATH. What exit status does the shell report? (integer, tolerance 0.5)
A process receives SIGTERM (15). Exit status reported for a killed process? (integer, tolerance 0.5)
File mode 0604 owned by alice, group robots, and Bob is in robots. Can Bob read it?
options: Yes: the other class grants read (4), so Bob can read
Yes: the group and other permissions are combined, giving read
No: Bob is in the file's group, so the group class (0) denies
Only if Bob is root, since only root can override the group
questions.explanation: Bob is in the file's group, so the group class (0) is the first match and denies; the other class is not consulted.

questions.prompt: `set -e` is on. Which line in a script does NOT stop it when it fails?
options: A failing command that stands on its own line in the script
A failing last command of the script, which sets the exit status
A failing command used as the condition of an if statement
A failing assignment from a command substitution on its own line
questions.explanation: Commands tested by if/while/&&/|| are exempt from errexit, a known exception.

questions.prompt: The command `ls /missing 2>&1 > out.txt` is run. Where does the error message go?
options: Into out.txt and the terminal, since 2>&1 duplicates it to both places
It is discarded, since the two redirections cancel each other out in effect
Into out.txt, since both streams are redirected to the file by the command
To the terminal: stderr was copied to the old stdout before stdout moved to the file
questions.explanation: 2>&1 is evaluated first, duplicating stderr onto the terminal.

questions.prompt: The pipeline `producer | filter | consumer` has stage statuses 3, 0, 0. With pipefail, what is the pipeline status? (integer, tolerance 0.5)
questions.explanation: pipefail returns the right-most non-zero status: 3. Without it: 0.

questions.prompt: Write a safe version of `cd $1; rm -rf *` and explain every change.
rubric: set -euo pipefail so failures stop the script.
Validate and quote the argument (dir=${1:?usage}; cd -- "$dir") and avoid a bare glob, e.g. rm -rf -- ./* only after a successful cd (or delete a named subdirectory).
Mentions testing the script on a scratch directory and refusing dangerous paths such as / or the home directory.
